decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core cardboard display range with visible prior launch commitment, management is likely to continue backing it and interpret any weak uptake as temporary rather than a reason to withdraw.

Because this pegboard-backed display sits near the firm's established offer and uses existing design and production capabilities, sunk development effort and public commitment favor keeping it on the market.
This quarter-pallet cardboard display is highly central to the firm's core display business, so escalation of commitment and strategic fit both make withdrawal unlikely.

Although somewhat more niche in format, it remains a core cardboard display product and the firm is likely to persist with it given prior investment and its relevance to the announced innovation-and-service strategy.

The wooden display pallet is somewhat less aligned with the paper-based core than the other launches, but management would still be inclined to retain it because it builds on the display offering and prior commitment can be justified as part of broadening solutions for retail customers.

Even with a narrower application in media products, it is still a close variant of the established quarter-pallet offer, so management is likely to continue it and attribute any disappointing demand to segment-specific or temporary factors.
